svg.title: Mathematical formulation of SEREP-integrated vibration control
svg.desc: Mathematical summary of Patel, Kumar and Ali's 2020 numerical SEREP-LQR beam study. Full second-order finite-element dynamics are reduced with a selected-mode, retained-coordinate transformation and congruence projection. The reduced displacement and velocity form a first-order state; a standard continuous-time Riccati equation produces reduced feedback. The reduced-designed actuator feedback is evaluated on the original full numerical model. The 402-degree,804-state full model is compared with 48nodes/96degrees for uniform selection and19nodes/38degrees retaining critical actuator junctions. Reported computational-cost reductions are95percent and97.5percent, respectively. The input/disturbance split and first-order Riccati notation are explanatory mathematical conventions, not a literal transcription of the paper. No full-order feedback gain lifting, experiment, or hardware validation is asserted.
svg.text: From coupled FE to reduced feedback.
Mathematical summary of the published numerical framework.
Eᵣ uses the same input mapping with B_d.
Check FRF, modes and controlled response.
Notation summary: q = physical displacement; F = B_u u + B_d d. Ψₘ = retained-coordinate rows; + = pseudoinverse.
State-space and Riccati equations use standard notation. No full-order gain-lifting map or experimental result is asserted.
Source: Patel, Kumar & Ali, IFAC-PapersOnLine 53(1), 51–56 (2020), Eqs. 10–21 and §5.1 · doi:10.1016/j.ifacol.2020.06.009
